title: A node author carries declared migration identifiers from authored planning source into the compiled node
description:
WRITER CHILD of task-122b55fd2c284174876bd1d5573bdcc5, filed by architect-dbe3631e 2026-09-07 under governor-afbde490's 20:30Z direction, which offered exactly this choice: "bounded scope amendment (fields + recursion + writer path + version/compatibility policy per DoD 3) OR a writer child with corrected DoD/deps". The writer child is the choice, because the authority half alone already occupies 9 files.

THE SPLIT, IN BUILD ORDER. task-122b55fd (this row's dependsOn) makes the durable node-authority format ABLE to carry a bounded migration declaration: the v3 roster member, its admission with duplicate REFUSAL, the version-scoped preimage so historical hashes never move, compose/project and the public export. THIS ROW makes an AUTHORED SOURCE able to state one and carry it through the compiler into that format. task-de65294bfa2649b99afc3aa4aa9399d0 then serves it over /runs/read and the browser decoder.

THE GAP, MEASURED AT HEAD 29f5d723 (re-measure before planning; global rail 6):
- `packages/scheduler/src/node-authority/node-planning-source-format.ts` (232 lines) - NODE_PLANNING_SOURCE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1 at :24, its own digest domain at :26, closed ENVELOPE_KEYS at :92 and DEPENDENCY_KEYS at :91. No migration member anywhere.
- `packages/scheduler/src/node-authority/node-planning-source-codec.ts` (232 lines) - exact-key decode and reconstruction; `sameNodePlanningSourceBytes` at :229 is the byte-identity comparator.
- `packages/scheduler/src/node-authority/node-planning-source-bounds.ts` (81 lines) - where a new bound belongs.
- `apps/daemon/src/planning/v2-compiler/scheduler-node-planning-authority.ts` (122 lines) - `SOURCE_KEYS` at :15-18 is an EXACT four-name roster checked by `exact(snapshot.value, SOURCE_KEYS)` at :85, and the draft at :98-119 is written out FIELD BY FIELD. Both must carry the declaration or it is dropped between the authored source and the authority draft, silently.
- `apps/daemon/src/planning/v2-compiler/authority-contracts.ts` (84 lines) - `V2CompilerNodeAuthorityRequest` carries no declaration.
- `apps/daemon/src/delivery-v2/node-planning-source-record.ts` - forwards admitted encoded bytes wholesale (worker-f72a1438 measured :86-97, :130-147, persistence :99), so it needs no rewrite, but that claim needs a test rather than an assumption.

Also measured and NOT this row's to change: `compiled-policy-authority-body.ts:102-126` and `journey-authority-bodies.ts:126-144` write explicit drafts too. Decide at planning time whether they must forward the member or may legitimately declare none, and SAY WHICH - do not leave a second silent drop path.

NOT IN SCOPE: the authority format itself (task-122b55fd owns the roster, the version policy, the preimage and the admission codes - consume them, do not redefine them), /runs/read and the browser decoder (task-de65294b), and the UI wording (task-78eedd8ebc2b43c581ac21ea28648a9a).
definitionOfDone: An AUTHORED planning source can state zero, one or several bounded migration identifiers, and the source's own format version, canonical bytes, digest domain and bounds all account for the member. The exact-key decoder refuses an unknown key and a malformed member with a stable code AND the layer that refused; a source that states none is DISTINCT from a legacy source that states nothing, carrying task-122b55fd's UNKNOWN-vs-explicit-empty distinction rather than collapsing both.

THE COMPILER FORWARDS IT, ASSERTED END TO END: a declaration stated in authored source reaches the compiled NodeDefinition through the PRODUCTION path (`readNodePlanningDefinition`), asserted BY VALUE on the resulting definition - not on a hand-built draft and not by calling the authority codec directly. `SOURCE_KEYS` (scheduler-node-planning-authority.ts:15-18) and the explicit draft (:98-119) both name the member; a test proves the member survives the `exact(...)` roster check that would otherwise reject the wider source.

THE SILENT-DROP PATHS ARE CLOSED AND NAMED. Every site that writes an explicit NodeDefinition draft is enumerated whole-tree (`compiled-policy-authority-body.ts`, `journey-authority-bodies.ts`, `scheduler-node-planning-authority.ts` at minimum) with a verdict per site: forwards the declaration, or legitimately declares none and says why in a comment at the site. A site that neither forwards nor states its choice is the defect this clause exists to prevent.

TWO IDENTIFIERS BOTH SURVIVE the source codec, the compiler and the resulting definition, asserted by value AND by count - a path that keeps only the first passes every single-identifier fixture. DUPLICATES ARE REFUSED, not deduplicated: assert the specific code and layer, and confirm the refusal comes from the intended layer rather than from a second admission arm downstream.

BYTE IDENTITY AND FORWARDING ARE PROVED, NOT ASSUMED: `sameNodePlanningSourceBytes` still answers correctly across the new member, and `delivery-v2/node-planning-source-record.ts` forwarding admitted bytes wholesale is asserted by a test rather than claimed from a reading.

MUTATION DRILL, quoted with its failing line: drop the member from `SOURCE_KEYS` (or from the explicit draft) and confirm the end-to-end arm from DoD 2 goes RED. Restore per global rail 13 - `git status --porcelain` the mutated paths first, and prove an untracked path's restore by sha256 against an out-of-tree backup in a call separate from the restore.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test` and `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` (this row spans both packages), plus `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` covers no apps/** file, so say that rather than quoting a bare root count line. Any new runtime module needs its one-line tracked `.js` bridge, and any new cross-package import needs the manifest dependency plus the lockfile importer entry.
taskRails: CONSUME task-122b55fd's AUTHORITY CONTRACT, DO NOT REDEFINE IT. The roster member name, its bound, its refusal codes, its layer and the UNKNOWN-vs-explicit-empty policy are that row's to set. If what landed does not fit this row's need, report blocked and have it amended - never mint a second spelling.

NO INFERENCE. A declaration is stated by the author or it does not exist. Never derive it from an objective, a filename, a diff, writeScopes or verifier output, and never default to an empty list at the output and call it authored (task-122b55fd rail 1).

ASSERT THROUGH THE PRODUCTION COMPILER PATH. `readNodePlanningDefinition` is the seam; a test that builds a draft by hand proves the authority codec works and proves nothing about the carrier this row exists to build.

DUPLICATES REFUSE, THEY DO NOT DEDUPLICATE. The generic scheduler list reader silently dedups and sorts (node-authority-fields.ts:76-77); do not reuse it for this member without confirming which behaviour task-122b55fd landed.
NO HISTORICAL REWRITE. An authored source that predates the member stays readable and keeps its bytes and its digest; do not migrate stored sources in place.

implementationPlan.description:
READ THE LANDED CONTRACT OFF DISK AND BASELINE. NO EDITS. The producer task-122b55fd LANDED as commit 4710d60b and is in REVIEW (not DONE), so your dependsOn gate opens only when QA approves it — but the contract is already on disk and you consume it VERBATIM (task rail 1). Confirm each of these; if any has MOVED because QA sent that row back, STOP AND REPORT rather than building to my citation:
(a) `grep -n 'declaredMigrations' packages/scheduler/src/node-authority/node-authority-contract.ts` — roster member at :100, and the type at :193 is `readonly declaredMigrations?: readonly string[]`, **OPTIONAL**. Absent = UNKNOWN, `[]` = the author declared none.
(b) `sed -n '95,118p' packages/scheduler/src/node-authority/node-authority-fields.ts` — `readDeclaredMigrations`. **AUTHORED ORDER IS PRESERVED, NOT SORTED**: it does `declared.push(identifier)` with no `.sort()`, and its own comment says the order is content that the digest binds. Your source layer must preserve authored order too, or two authored spellings collapse into one identity.
(c) THE EXACT REFUSAL VOCABULARY you must not re-mint: duplicate -> `NODE_AUTHORITY_DUPLICATE_MIGRATION` @ `NODE_AUTHORITY_ADMISSION` (:112-113); non-list and inadmissible entry -> `NODE_AUTHORITY_FIELD_INVALID` @ `NODE_AUTHORITY_ADMISSION` (:99-101, :110-111); over-bound -> `NODE_AUTHORITY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` @ `NODE_AUTHORITY_LIMITS` (:103-105). The bound is `maxMigrationEntries: 64` (contract.ts:154) and entries are admitted by `asId`.
(d) `sed -n '120,132p' packages/scheduler/src/node-authority/node-authority-codec.ts` — **THE VERSION IS CHOSEN BY CONTENT, NEVER STATED BY A CALLER**: `minted = draft.declaredMigrations === undefined ? NODE_AUTHORITY_UNDECLARED_SCHEMA_VERSION : NODE_AUTHORITY_SCHEMA_VERSION`. `node-authority-recursion.ts:205,220` selects the preimage roster by PRESENCE for the same reason. **THIS IS THE PATTERN YOUR SOURCE LAYER COPIES**, one level up — do not invent a second one (task rail 1).
(e) `grep -n 'declaredMigrations' packages/scheduler/src/node-authority/node-authority-fields.ts packages/scheduler/src/node-authority/node-authority-compose.ts` — both spread conditionally (`...(x === undefined ? {} : { declaredMigrations: x })`, fields.ts:290-292, compose.ts:249-250). **An assigned `undefined` is not an absent key** once `Object.keys` runs, and the codec byte-compares its own re-encode. Do the same in the source layer.
BASELINE, quoted with `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test` (this row edits scheduler files). Do not run the daemon leg yet — step 7 owns it. Disclose and attribute any peer red.

THE ARMS FIRST, RED BEFORE ANY PRODUCTION EDIT.
IN `packages/scheduler/src/node-authority/node-planning-source-codec.test.ts` (382 lines, existing):
(a) **BYTE IDENTITY OF A LEGACY SOURCE** — the sharpest hazard, exactly as it was one layer down. Encode/decode an existing source that declares nothing and assert the bytes and `sourceDigest` are EXACTLY unchanged, and that the member is ABSENT from the decoded content (`"declaredMigrations" in content` is false, NOT `toEqual([])`). A defaulted `[]` would move every stored source's digest and mint a declaration nobody authored (task rail 2).
(b) **ROUND TRIP BY VALUE AND BY COUNT** with TWO identifiers, and **IN AUTHORED ORDER** — assert the exact array, not a sorted or set-compared one, because the landed authority preserves order as content (step 1(b)). A path keeping only the first passes every single-identifier fixture (DoD 4).
(c) **EXPLICIT EMPTY IS DISTINCT FROM ABSENT** (DoD 1): a source stating `[]` decodes with the member PRESENT and empty, and its `sourceDigest` differs from the same source encoding nothing.
(d) **THE DECODER STAYS EXACT-KEY**: an unknown key still refuses, and a malformed member (non-list, non-string entry, over-bound, duplicate) refuses with its stable code AND the layer that refused. Assert the LAYER too — the source layer and the authority layer can both say a value is bad, and an arm that only checks a code cannot tell which one answered (global rail 1).
(e) **`sameNodePlanningSourceBytes` still answers correctly** across the member (DoD 5): equal for identical declarations, unequal for different ones and for declared-none vs absent.
IN A NEW FILE `apps/daemon/src/planning/v2-compiler/scheduler-node-planning-authority.test.ts` — new because NOTHING in the tree drives `readNodePlanningDefinition` today (`git grep -ln readNodePlanningDefinition -- 'apps/**'` returns only the two production modules), which is precisely why this member could be dropped between the source and the draft without a single test noticing:
(f) **THE END-TO-END ARM (DoD 2), and the row's whole point.** Drive the PRODUCTION `readNodePlanningDefinition` with a reader returning a source that declares two identifiers, and assert them BY VALUE on the returned `NodeDefinition.declaredMigrations`. Not on a hand-built draft, not by calling the authority codec directly (task rail 3).
(g) **THE ROSTER ARM**: the same call with a source that declares NOTHING still succeeds and the returned definition has NO `declaredMigrations` key — this is what proves the widened `exact(...)` check did not become mandatory and break every existing authored source.
(h) **THE DROP ARM**: assert the definition's `schemaVersion` differs between the declaring and non-declaring cases, so a forward that silently loses the member cannot pass by returning a valid definition.
A test file needs no `.js` bridge; only runtime modules do. Run both files and quote the failing lines.

THE SOURCE FORMAT — `packages/scheduler/src/node-authority/node-planning-source-format.ts` (232 lines; keep under 300).
(1) **THE MEMBER, OPTIONAL**: add `readonly declaredMigrations?: readonly string[]` to `NodePlanningSourceContent` (:64-70). Optional for the same reason it is optional one layer down: absent = the source predates the member or declares nothing knowable, `[]` = the author declared none. Comment it, because `authority-contracts.ts` derives `V2CompilerNodePlanningAuthority = Omit<NodePlanningSourceContent, "version">` from this type and the compiler reads that shape.
(2) **VERSION BY PRESENCE, COPYING THE LANDED PATTERN** (step 1(d)): keep `NODE_PLANNING_SOURCE_SCHEMA_VERSION` as the current version and add an UNDECLARED version constant plus per-version tag and digest-domain lookups — v1 keeps `MOE-NODE-PLANNING-SOURCE/1` and `MOE-NODE-PLANNING-SOURCE-CONTENT-HASH/1` BYTE FOR BYTE, the new version gets its own pair. A source is minted at the LOWEST version that can carry it, chosen by whether it states the member — never by a caller-supplied version, which is how a declaring source would get framed with the old tag.
(3) **NO NEW BOUND IS NEEDED.** This module already imports `NODE_AUTHORITY_LIMITS` (:20); reuse `maxMigrationEntries` (64) and the same `asId`-shaped entry admission, so the source and the authority agree by construction rather than by two bounds that can drift. Do NOT edit `node-planning-source-bounds.ts` — state that you checked and why it needs nothing.
(4) **REFUSALS**: if the source layer needs its own duplicate/oversize code, add it to `NODE_PLANNING_SOURCE_CODES` (:28) rather than reusing an authority code in a source-layer refusal — arm 2(d) asserts WHICH layer answered, and two layers sharing one code makes that arm unable to discriminate.

THE SOURCE CODEC — `packages/scheduler/src/node-authority/node-planning-source-codec.ts` (232 lines; keep under 300).
(1) **THE KEY ROSTERS ADMIT IT OPTIONALLY.** `CONTENT_KEYS = [...DRAFT_KEYS, "version"]` at :54 and the check at :86-87 (`hasOnlyOwnStringKeys` PLUS every key present) make every roster member REQUIRED. Widening the roster alone therefore refuses every existing source. Admit the member as OPTIONAL: present-and-admissible, or absent — and a present-but-`undefined` value is NOT absent, so decide which you accept and refuse the other rather than letting both through.
(2) **THE WIRE ENVELOPE.** `ENVELOPE_KEYS` (:92) is `[acceptanceCriterionContentBytesBase64, dependencyContentBytesBase64, planExecutionContentBytesBase64, schema]` — three base64 content blobs plus the schema tag. DECIDE AND COMMENT AT THE SITE where the declaration rides: its own optional envelope key, or inside the dependency blob beside `directHardDependencies`/`predicateRegistry` (`DEPENDENCY_KEYS`, :91). Either is defensible; leaving it implicit is not, because the envelope is the durable wire and a later reader has to know. Whichever you choose, the v1 envelope for a non-declaring source must serialize to the SAME BYTES it does today.
(3) **ENCODE STAMPS THE SOURCE'S OWN VERSION AND TAG**, selected by presence per step 3(2) — not the module's current constant. Arm 2(a) is what catches this.
(4) **RECONSTRUCTION CARRIES IT THROUGH** (the decode-side rebuild, ~:180-185) using conditional spread, never an assigned `undefined` (step 1(e)).
Run `node-planning-source-codec.test.ts`. Arms (a) through (e) must now be green.

THE COMPILER FORWARD — `apps/daemon/src/planning/v2-compiler/scheduler-node-planning-authority.ts` (122 lines). This is the drop point the row exists to close, and BOTH halves are needed: either alone loses the member silently.
(1) **`SOURCE_KEYS` (:15-18) MUST ADMIT IT WITHOUT REQUIRING IT.** `exact(value, keys)` (snapshot.ts:70-74) tests own-key COUNT equality plus every key present — so adding a fifth name makes the member MANDATORY and refuses every existing authored source. Accept either roster: the four required names, or those four plus `declaredMigrations`. Do NOT widen `exact` itself — it is used across this package and loosening it would relax unrelated boundary checks.
(2) **THE EXPLICIT DRAFT (:98-119) FORWARDS IT.** The draft is written field by field, so a member nobody assigns is dropped with no error. Add it with conditional spread — `...(snapshot.value["declaredMigrations"] === undefined ? {} : { declaredMigrations: snapshot.value["declaredMigrations"] })` — never as an assigned `undefined`, which `readDraftFields` and the codec's byte comparison both treat differently from an absent key.
(3) **DO NOT TOUCH `matchesRequest`** unless arm 2(f) forces it. If it reds because the created definition no longer matches the request, report what it compares before changing it — that function is the guard that the compiled node is the one that was asked for, and loosening it to make a test pass would be the wrong repair.
(4) The member rides the SOURCE, not `V2CompilerNodeAuthorityRequest`. That is deliberate and measured: `authority-contracts.ts:72` already calls `V2CompilerNodePlanningAuthority` "source-owned planning/dependency material", `directHardDependencies` rides the source for the same reason, and putting it on the request instead would drag the product contract, `NodeFact` and `V2CompiledNode` into this row. Write that sentence at the site so the next reader does not re-litigate it.
Run arm 2(f), (g), (h).

CLOSE THE OTHER SILENT-DROP PATHS WITH A VERDICT EACH (DoD 3). `git grep -n 'draft: {' -- 'apps/**/*.ts' 'packages/**/*.ts' ':!*.test.ts'` returns NINE sites; six are fixtures. **THE THREE PRODUCTION SITES ARE**: `apps/daemon/src/planning/v2-compiler/scheduler-node-planning-authority.ts:100` (step 5), `apps/daemon/src/planning/compiled-policy-authority-body.ts:104`, and `apps/daemon/src/planning/journey-authority-bodies.ts:128`. Re-run that grep at your HEAD and correct me if it has changed.
FOR EACH OF THE TWO REMAINING SITES, decide and WRITE THE VERDICT AS A COMMENT AT THE SITE — not in the completion record, where the next reader will not find it:
- **FORWARDS IT**, if that body composes a node whose author could have declared migrations; then add the conditional spread exactly as step 5(2) does, and add an arm.
- **OR LEGITIMATELY DECLARES NONE**, if the body is synthesized by the daemon rather than authored — in which case say WHY in the comment ("this body is minted by X, which has no author to state a declaration; absent is therefore correct and is NOT the same as `[]`"). Absent, not `[]` — defaulting to empty would mint a false declaration (task rail 2).
A SITE THAT NEITHER FORWARDS NOR STATES ITS CHOICE IS THE DEFECT THIS CLAUSE EXISTS TO PREVENT. "It did not need one" without a reason is not a verdict.
The six fixture sites need no verdict; name them and say they are fixtures rather than leaving them uncounted.

DRILLS, GATES, SELF-REVIEW. Load `adversarial-self-review` and read your own diff as an attacker first.
DRILLS — `git status --porcelain` the mutated paths FIRST and record the output. `scheduler-node-planning-authority.test.ts` is NEW and therefore UNTRACKED, so `git diff` is blind to it and certifies nothing: back it up out of tree (%TEMP%, suffixed with your worker id) and prove its restore by SHA256 equality in a call SEPARATE from the restore (global rail 13). The other six paths are tracked; an empty `git diff -- <path>` in a separate call is valid proof for those. State which path fell in which class.
THREE DRILLS, each quoted with its failing line:
(i) **THE ROW'S REASON FOR EXISTING** (DoD 6): drop `declaredMigrations` from the explicit draft at scheduler-node-planning-authority.ts:98-119, leaving `SOURCE_KEYS` widened. Confirm arm 2(f) goes RED. If it stays green, the arm is asserting the source rather than the compiled definition and must be rewritten — that is the exact hole this row was filed to close.
(ii) **THE MANDATORY-KEY DRILL**: make the member REQUIRED in `SOURCE_KEYS` (a single five-name roster). Confirm arm 2(g) reds — a non-declaring source must still compile, or every authored source in the store stops compiling.
(iii) **THE FALSE-DECLARATION DRILL**: default the member to `[]` in the source codec's reconstruction. Confirm arm 2(a) reds on byte or digest inequality. That is the mutation a well-meaning refactor makes, and it mints a declaration nobody authored.
GATES — standalone and foreground, ONE command per call, no pipes and no `;` chains, each quoted with its `Test Files N passed` count line, because an exit-0 leg with NO count line ran nothing (global rail 8): `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test`, then `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` (this row spans both packages), then `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` covers no `apps/**` file — say that rather than quoting it. The daemon leg is slow (~22 min) and flaky on this branch: attribute any red outside this row's seven files against your step 1 baseline and disclose foreign red verbatim rather than owning it or calling it green.
NO NEW CROSS-PACKAGE IMPORT IS INTRODUCED: `apps/daemon` already depends on `@moe/scheduler` (authority-contracts.ts imports `NodePlanningSourceContent` from it today), so no manifest or lockfile edit is needed — state that you checked rather than leaving DoD 7's edge clause looking skipped. Likewise state that no new runtime module was created, so no `.js` bridge was owed.
SELF-REVIEW AND RECORD, in completionSummary plus one row comment for detail over the cap: where the declaration rides on the wire and why (step 4(2)); that authored ORDER is preserved rather than sorted, matching the landed authority; the two verdicts from step 6 with their reasons; confirmation that a non-declaring source still compiles unchanged and byte-identical; the three drill outcomes with their failing lines; and the exact spelling and refusal vocabulary you consumed from task-122b55fd, so task-de65294b builds against the same one. Named verification command: `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test`.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
THE PRODUCER ALREADY LANDED WHILE THIS ROW SAT IN PLANNING, so nothing here is planned against an unbuilt symbol. task-122b55fd landed as commit 4710d60b and is in REVIEW with qa-97200064; `declaredMigrations` is on disk with its bound, its refusal vocabulary and its version policy. I read all of it rather than restating my own plan for that row — and the worker made ONE refinement I did not specify and which is better: the version is selected by CONTENT/PRESENCE (`draft.declaredMigrations === undefined ? UNDECLARED : CURRENT`, codec.ts:127-128; recursion.ts:220 selects the preimage roster the same way) rather than by a stated version. That means a body declaring nothing is never promoted and never moves its identity. THIS ROW COPIES THAT PATTERN ONE LEVEL UP rather than inventing a second one (task rail 1).

WHERE THE DECLARATION RIDES WAS THE ROW'S ONE REAL DESIGN QUESTION, and I measured it rather than assuming the DoD I wrote was right. Two candidates: `V2CompilerNodeAuthorityRequest` (which carries `constraints`, `resources`, `readScopes`, `writeScopes` — node attributes) or `NodePlanningSourceContent` (the authored source). I chose THE SOURCE, for three measured reasons: `authority-contracts.ts:72` already calls `V2CompilerNodePlanningAuthority = Omit<NodePlanningSourceContent,"version">` "source-owned planning/dependency material"; `directHardDependencies` — also a NodeDefinition field — rides the source for exactly that reason; and the request is built from `V2CompiledNode` (assembly.ts:116-143), which is derived from `NodeFact` and the product contract, so putting the member there would drag the product-contract schema, its codec, its digest, admission, NodeFact and V2CompiledNode into this row. The row's own DoD 1 also says the SOURCE's format version, canonical bytes, digest domain and bounds must account for the member, which only makes sense on the source. Step 5(4) has the worker write that reasoning at the site so it is not re-litigated.

THE END-TO-END ARM NEEDS A NEW TEST FILE, and the reason is itself the finding: `git grep -ln readNodePlanningDefinition -- 'apps/**'` returns ONLY the two production modules. **Nothing in the tree drives that function.** That is precisely why a member can be dropped between the authored source and the authority draft without a single test noticing, and it is why DoD 2 insists the arm run through the production path rather than a hand-built draft.

REJECTED — widening `exact()` in snapshot.ts to take an optional-key list. It is used across the v2-compiler package for boundary checks, and loosening it would relax unrelated rosters to make one call site convenient. Step 5(1) accepts either of two exact rosters instead, which is local and reversible.

REJECTED — editing `node-planning-source-bounds.ts`. The source format module already imports `NODE_AUTHORITY_LIMITS` (:20), so reusing `maxMigrationEntries` (64) makes the source and the authority agree by construction. A second bound is two numbers that can drift apart.

REJECTED — releasing this row and waiting for the producer to reach DONE. dependsOn gates WORKING claims, not planning, and the contract is already readable at HEAD. Step 1 makes the worker re-read it and STOP if QA sent that row back and it moved.
